descriptors.definition: External Funding Requirement determines the amount of capital a firm must raise externally to support a targeted increase in sales while respecting specific financial constraints. It can be computed through balance sheet item analysis or through formula-based approaches incorporating spontaneous liabilities, profit margins, and retained earnings.
inclusion: Calculation of total asset increases linked to sales growth
Spontaneous liabilities that vary directly with sales
Retained earnings based on net profit margin and dividend payout ratio
exclusion: Internal equity generation without external capital procurement
Sustainable growth rate computations that assume constant financial policies
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from Sustainable Growth Rate because EFR calculates exact monetary funding deficits when specific structural ratios or growth targets are mandated rather than maximum unconstrained growth.
